rule: Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, ...) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. ... Call on a computed receiver (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` ... an external type is qualified through its explicit import.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. ArrayList is outside the scan and qualified through `import java.util.ArrayList` (generic argument dropped), so super(capacity) is java.util.ArrayList#<init>, medium. `super.add(..)` and `super.toString()` call through `super` whose superclass (ArrayList; implicit java.lang.Object for Plain) is not in the scan: `.member`, low. `s` is a parameter declared String (java.lang implicitly imported, Decisions 2026-10-29), so java.lang.String#trim, medium.
